sections.title: Why Invest?
bullets: Steady Q1FY27 as a strong India hospital print was partially offset by higher losses in NHIC and lower overseas margins.
Primarily aided by further improvement in case/payor mix, we bake in 15%/14% India hospital sales/EBITDA CAGRs over FY26-29E.
Led by a continued ramp-up in the Camana Bay Hospital and lower losses in the insurance business and a better margin profile for PPG, we bake in a healthy ~22% overall EBITDA CAGR over FY26-29E.
While largely debt-funded foray in UK does raise eyebrows, NARH unable to repatriate cash generated in Cayman to its India entity without incurring tax liabilities.
Q1FY27 sales of ~Rs2680 cr (+78% yoy) were 2% ahead of our estimates.
India hospital revenues grew by 16% yoy in Q1FY27 to ~Rs1290 cr.
We expect NARH to report an India ARPOB CAGR of ~6% over FY26-29E, aided by a better surgical mix and ongoing payor mix changes.
Majority of NARH’s upcoming bed additions are in its core markets, thereby limiting execution risks.
Cayman hospitals growing at 15% yoy led by the Camana Bay hospital and insurance sales surging ~3X yoy.

abbreviations: (NHIC – Narayana Health Insurance Company | CAGR – Compound Annual Growth Rate | ARPOB – Average Revenue Per Occupied Bed | EBITDA – Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation & Amortization)
